narrative.overview:
Each house is a passbook. Every bill is one printed entry line: the date and the amount set by the
passbook printer in fixed columns, what it is written in plain sans-serif between them, the amount
flush right. A state (estimated, replaced, archived) is a rubber stamp on the line, in violet stamp
ink, never a coloured badge. The shell (bottom bar, sidebar, the house's cover band, the sign-in
band) is bottle-green book cloth with a faint woven texture; the page is pale green-grey security
paper. The dark theme is the closed book: cloth-dark ground, paper-light ink — designed, not
inverted.

Density is that of a bank statement read on a phone: compact lines, figures in aligned columns,
hierarchy by weight, tracking and rules rather than by size. Nothing competes with the numbers:
no shadows, no hero figures, no illustration. The one authored motion is the stamp landing.
keyCharacteristics: Security-tinted paper page, bottle-green cloth shell, near-black print ink.
Courier Prime for figures only; Libre Franklin for everything else.
Hairline office rules; 2 px corners on controls, 4 px on panels; no shadows.
Violet stamp ink reserved for states and non-blocking warnings; danger red reserved for errors and destructive actions.
Light and dark both designed from the same token names.

rules.name: The Tokens Only Rule
rules.body: Tailwind's default palette is reset (`--color-*: initial`); only the tokens above and in Charts exist. No literal colour in a component, ever (the logo SVG is the one asset with baked-in values, equal to the tokens).

rules.name: The Closed Book Rule
rules.body: Dark comes only from redefining the same variables under `[data-theme='dark']` and, for the `system` cookie, under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`. Never use Tailwind's `dark:` variant: it ignores the theme cookie. A new token goes into `@theme` and into both dark blocks, and into this file.

rules.name: The Stamp Ink Rule
rules.body: Violet is for states and non-blocking warnings only: the three stamps, arithmetic warnings, the overlap choice, a reading that looks wrong (and the focus ring that shares its ink). A violet button, heading or icon is a defect.

rules.name: The Red Means Danger Rule
rules.body: `danger` marks errors and destructive actions, nothing else; a warning that does not block is stamp ink, not red.

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: A chart token means one thing. Reusing `cat-commodity` for an unrelated series because "blue looks nice" breaks the reading across charts.

rules.name: The Printer Rule
rules.body: Courier Prime sets figures only — dates, amounts, quantities, readings, identifiers. Never a sentence, a label, a heading or a button.

rules.name: The No Giant Numbers Rule
rules.body: Rank by weight, tracking and rules, not by size. No balance hero, no figure above 24 px; an amount is as large as the line it prints on.

rules.name: The Flat Page Rule
rules.body: No `box-shadow`, no blur, no glow. If something needs to stand apart, give it a rule or a different paper tone.

rules.name: The One Motion Rule
rules.body: The stamp press is the only authored motion. No page transitions, no hover lifts, no animated counters.

dos: **Do** use only the tokens in this file; add a new one to `@theme`, to both dark blocks and here.
**Do** build controls from the shared classes (`buttonClass`, `inputClass`, `figureInputClass`, `panelClass`, `columnHeaderClass`) rather than restating their utilities.
**Do** set every date, amount, quantity, reading and identifier with the `figures` utility, and align amounts flush right.
**Do** put the shell on cloth (`cloth` utility) and the content on paper, and draw focus in `on-brand` on cloth.
**Do** keep text contrast at or above 4.5:1 in both themes, and give every chart direct labels or its data table.
**Do** use 2 px corners on controls and 4 px on containers, and 1 px rules (the column-header underline, outlined buttons and stamps excepted).
**Do** confirm a destructive act in the app's own dialog, saying what it removes.
donts: **Don't** make it look like a supplier's app: no energetic green/orange branding, no light bulbs, no flames as brand, no happy-family photos.
**Don't** make it a grey 2000s back office: no flat grey everywhere, no dense tables without hierarchy.
**Don't** go cream-and-serif: the paper is cool green-grey and the type is sans plus Courier.
**Don't** build white rounded cards with a blue balance hero.
**Don't** put kicker or eyebrow labels above headings.
**Don't** put coloured side borders thicker than 1 px on panels, lines or warnings (the 2 px active tick of a nav item is the shell's own mark, not a side border).
**Don't** use shadows, Tailwind's `dark:` variant, or literal colours in components.
**Don't** use violet for anything but states and non-blocking warnings, or red for anything but errors and destructive actions.
**Don't** set prose, labels or buttons in Courier Prime, or any functional text below 11 px.
**Don't** use real personal data in examples: invented figures and generic names only (Casa Fenicottero, Fenicottero Energia).
